summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a left total knee replacement due to severe degenerative joint disease. The surgery was performed on 2160-01-30 and proceeded without complications. Postoperatively, she developed acute posthemorrhagic anemia requiring four units of packed red blood cells over two days. Her renal function was closely monitored given her history of kidney transplant, and she was seen by nephrology. A urinary tract infection caused by E. coli, sensitive to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, was identified and treated. Pain was managed initially with a PCA pump, transitioning to oral acetaminophen and hydromorphone. She received Lovenox for DVT prophylaxis and was started on warfarin at discharge with instructions for INR monitoring. Physical therapy began on postoperative day one, and she achieved weight-bearing as tolerated. The wound was clean and healing without signs of infection. She was discharged home with home health services and detailed instructions on wound care, anticoagulation, and follow-up.
